Problem: What is the residue modulo $16$ of the sum of the modulo $16$ inverses of the first $8$ positive odd integers?

Express your answer as an integer from $0$ to $15$, inclusive.

message.content:
The first 8 positive odd integers are:

\[
1,3,5,7,9,11,13,15
\]

Their inverses modulo \(16\) are:

\[
\begin{aligned}
1^{-1} &\equiv 1 \\
3^{-1} &\equiv 11 \quad (3\cdot 11=33\equiv 1) \\
5^{-1} &\equiv 13 \quad (5\cdot 13=65\equiv 1) \\
7^{-1} &\equiv 7 \quad (7\cdot 7=49\equiv 1) \\
9^{-1} &\equiv 9 \quad (9\cdot 9=81\equiv 1) \\
11^{-1} &\equiv 3 \\
13^{-1} &\equiv 5 \\
15^{-1} &\equiv 15 \quad (15\equiv -1)
\end{aligned}
\]

Summing them:

\[
1+11+13+7+9+3+5+15=64
\]

Modulo \(16\):

\[
64 \equiv 0 \pmod{16}
\]

The answer is 0.
